newsitem.title: UK: British consumers cautious despite boom - survey.
newsitem.headline: British consumers cautious despite boom - survey.

text.p: British consumers are worried about money, cautious about their personal finances and wary of running up debts, a new survey said on Saturday.

American Express said consumer confidence or the feel-good factor' appears to hang in the balance with 27 percent of people surveyed saying their spending power has diminished over the past year and only 21 percent saying they are better off.
The rest say their circumstances have not changed.

"Our survey provides an interesting comparison with recent reports of consumer spending growth by showing that there is an underlying caution in consumer spending patterns," said American Express accountant John Calverley.
"The findings indicate a realistic and measured approach to personal finances among today's consumers. This is in stark contrast to the over confident spend culture of the 1980s."
The survey was compiled using interviews with 763 adults carried out by the British Market Research Bureau International.
It found 76 percent of consumers would rather go without than take out a bank loan or overdraft and 86 percent buy only what they can afford.
